content.title: About
content.content: White wine is made from white or light‑colored grapes, and also from dark varieties that are pressed without skins. It displays a pale golden to light‑green hue and a characteristic fruity aroma with notes of citrus, apple, pear, and sometimes tropical fruits. The taste is usually light, refreshing, with moderate acidity and a soft tannic structure.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The earliest references to white wine date back to ancient Rome, where it was prized for its lightness and ability to quench thirst in hot weather.
The most famous white wine grape is Chardonnay, cultivated in more than 70 countries worldwide.
Sauvignon Blanc wines often exhibit distinctive green pepper and herbaceous notes.
Traditional "méthode champenoise" (secondary fermentation in the bottle) is used not only for sparkling wines but also for some white wines, giving them a fine mousse.
White wine is frequently used in cooking for sauces, marinades, and desserts because its acidity enhances flavors.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Phenolic compounds and resveratrol in white wine help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: May modestly reduce cardiovascular risk
items.content: Moderate intake (150‑200 ml per day) can improve lipid profiles and raise HDL‑cholesterol levels.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Mild acidity stimulates gastric juice production, aiding the digestion of meals.

items.title: Provides B‑vitamins
items.content: White wines, especially those from fresh grapes, contain thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin.

items.title: Mild diuretic effect
items.content: Water and a small amount of alcohol promote the elimination of excess fluids.

items.title: Alcohol effects
items.content: Excessive consumption can lead to dependence, liver damage, and other health issues.

items.title: Sulfite allergy
items.content: Sulfites used as preservatives may trigger reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Alcohol can amplify the effects of certain medications, including anticoagulants and diabetes drugs.

items.title: Caloric content
items.content: White wine contains about 80 kcal per 100 ml, so it should be accounted for in daily energy balance.

items.title: Not recommended for pregnant women
items.content: Alcohol may adversely affect fetal development; pregnant women should abstain completely.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve white wine chilled (8‑12 °C) in narrow‑rimmed glasses to concentrate the aroma. It pairs well with seafood, light salads, chicken in creamy sauces, and soft cheeses. In cooking, use it in sauces, marinades, and desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bottle in a cool, dark place, stored horizontally so the cork stays moist. After opening, consume within 3‑5 days, sealing tightly and refrigerating.
